tasks.d:
**1 Models and entailment in propositional logic**

For each of the following statements, determine whether it is true or not by building the complete model (truth table). *Hint: you can add the full statement as a column in the table by replacing the “entails” ( ⊨ ) symbol by an “implies” ( ⇒ ) symbol.*
tasks.fasit:
- **a) Sant.** Bare raden A = F, B = F gjør ¬A ∧ ¬B sann, og der er ¬B også sann.
- **b) Usant.** Motmodell A = F, B = T: ¬A ∨ ¬B er sann, men ¬B er usann.
- **c) Sant.** Bare raden A = F, B = T gjør ¬A ∧ B sann, og der er A ∨ B sann.
- **d) Usant.** Motmodell A = F, B = T: A ⇒ B er sann, men A ⇔ B er usann.
- **e) Sant.** A ∨ ¬B ∨ C er usann bare i A = F, B = T, C = F, og der er venstresiden usann (A ⇒ B = T, C = F).
- **f) Sant (satisfiable).** A = T, B = F gjør begge leddene sanne.
- **g) Usant (unsatisfiable).** A ∧ ¬B krever A = T, B = F, og da er ¬A ⇔ ¬B usann.

α ⊨ β holder nøyaktig når α ⇒ β er sann i hver rad. Satisfiable betyr sann i minst én rad. Rader som bryter, er i fet skrift.

a) ¬A ∧ ¬B ⊨ ¬B

| A | B | ¬A ∧ ¬B | ¬B | (¬A ∧ ¬B) ⇒ ¬B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | F | T |
| T | F | F | T | T |
| T | T | F | F | T |

b) ¬A ∨ ¬B ⊨ ¬B

| A | B | ¬A ∨ ¬B | ¬B | (¬A ∨ ¬B) ⇒ ¬B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | T | T | T |
| **F** | **T** | **T** | **F** | **F** |
| T | F | T | T | T |
| T | T | F | F | T |

c) ¬A ∧ B ⊨ A ∨ B

| A | B | ¬A ∧ B | A ∨ B | (¬A ∧ B) ⇒ (A ∨ B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | F | F | T |
| F | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | F | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | T |

d) A ⇒ B ⊨ A ⇔ B

| A | B | A ⇒ B | A ⇔ B | (A ⇒ B) ⇒ (A ⇔ B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | T | T | T |
| **F** | **T** | **T** | **F** | **F** |
| T | F | F | F | T |
| T | T | T | T | T |

e) (A ⇒ B) ⇔ C ⊨ A ∨ ¬B ∨ C

| A | B | C | A ⇒ B | (A ⇒ B) ⇔ C | A ∨ ¬B ∨ C | ⇒-kolonnen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | F | T | F | T | T |
| F | F | T | T | T | T | T |
| F | T | F | T | F | F | T |
| F | T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | F | F | T | T | T |
| T | F | T | F | F | T | T |
| T | T | F | T | F | T | T |
| T | T | T | T | T | T | T |

f) (¬A ⇒ ¬B) ∧ (A ∧ ¬B)

| A | B | ¬A ⇒ ¬B | A ∧ ¬B | Hele setningen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | T | F | F |
| F | T | F | F | F |
| **T** | **F** | **T** | **T** | **T** |
| T | T | T | F | F |

g) (¬A ⇔ ¬B) ∧ (A ∧ ¬B)

| A | B | ¬A ⇔ ¬B | A ∧ ¬B | Hele setningen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | F | T | F | F |
| F | T | F | F | F |
| T | F | F | T | F |
| T | T | T | F | F |

Vanlig feil: å kreve like kolonner for ⊨. Det er ekvivalens. For entailment ser du bare på radene der venstresiden er sann.

*Kilde: notatet til E11 (A4 1.1 a og Fasit Øv selv 1–2). Ingen offisiell fasit for A4. Kontroll: alle tabellene er regnet ut med eget skript.*

tasks.d:
The Bio Space Lab orbiting Earth suffered an electrical anomaly, leading to severe damage in some of its sectors. One of the most affected sectors was Sector 4 (VANN), which holds aquatic and marine specimens of our planet in its tanks. HQ has assigned you the task to implement a control system for the 32 tanks in the sector while maintenance and repairs are being carried out. Each tank has three sensors: (*S*1) A **motion detection** sensor to know whether if there are specimens in the tank or if it is empty (*S*2) A **toxicity level** detector (*S*3) An **electrical charge** meter For Sensors *S*2 and *S*3, the signal is marked as ‘high’ after a certain threshold. Tanks send updates to the control mechanism once every minute, using an 8-byte packet that looks like this:

01000111

where the first three bits (in red above) represent the reading of the sensors (motion, toxicity and electrical charge; in this order). The remaining five bits (in blue above) are used for representing the ID of the tank (in binary encoding). HQ has notified you that a tank gate should be closed if **any** of the following situations arise: (*C*1) If species inside are safe (low toxicity and low electric charge). (*C*2) If the tank is unoccupied and water toxicity is high. (*C*3) If the electrical charge level in a tank is marked as ‘dangerous’, no matter if it is inhabited or its toxicity. For the remaining cases, energy should be saved and normal flow is to be expected. Your task is to design a control system using model checking to close tank gates whenever an 8-bit packet arrives: a) Generate the vocabulary of the system b) Express all closing conditions (*C*1, *C*2, *C*3) for the gates as propositional logic statements c) Write the complete model (truth table) of the system d) Write an example packet and explain what the packet means in terms of the control system *Merknad:* «8-byte packet» er en skrivefeil i originalen. Pakken har 3 + 5 = 8 biter.
f: b) C1, C2 og C3 som utsagn i proposisjonslogikk
d) Eksempelpakke og hva den betyr
tasks.fasit:
**a) Vokabular:** M = motion detected (tanken har dyr), T = toxicity high, E = electrical charge high (dangerous), Close = tankporten skal lukkes. Med ID-en blir det M<sub>i</sub>, T<sub>i</sub>, E<sub>i</sub> og Close<sub>i</sub> for tank i = 0, …, 31. ID-bitene velger bare hvilken tank symbolene gjelder.

**b) Lukkebetingelsene:**
- C1: ¬T ∧ ¬E ⇒ Close (dyrene er trygge: lav toksisitet og lav ladning)
- C2: ¬M ∧ T ⇒ Close (tom tank og høy toksisitet)
- C3: E ⇒ Close (farlig ladning, uansett M og T)

Alle andre tilfeller gir normal flow, så hele systemet er Close ⇔ (¬T ∧ ¬E) ∨ (¬M ∧ T) ∨ E. Tabellen viser at det forenkles til Close ⇔ ¬M ∨ ¬T ∨ E, altså ¬Close ⇔ M ∧ T ∧ ¬E.

**c) Hele modellen** (bitene i samme rekkefølge som i pakken):

| M | T | E | C1 | C2 | C3 | Close |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 | T | F | F | T |
| 0 | 0 | 1 | F | F | T | T |
| 0 | 1 | 0 | F | T | F | T |
| 0 | 1 | 1 | F | T | T | T |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | T | F | F | T |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | F | F | T | T |
| **1** | **1** | **0** | **F** | **F** | **F** | **F** |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | F | F | T | T |

Med de 5 ID-bitene blir den fulle tabellen 2⁸ = 256 rader, men de 8 radene over gjentas for hver tank.

**d) Eksempelpakke:** Pakken fra oppgaven, 010 00111, betyr M = 0, T = 1, E = 0 for tank 00111₂ = 7. Tanken er tom og har høy toksisitet, så C2 slår til, og porten til tank 7 lukkes. Pakken 110 00011 betyr at tank 3 har dyr, høy toksisitet og lav ladning. Ingen betingelse slår til, så porten holdes åpen med normal flow. Kontrollsystemet gjør model checking: det ser på raden som passer med sensorverdiene og sjekker om KB ∧ M ∧ T ∧ ¬E ⊨ Close.

Tolkning: «species inside are safe» kan også leses som M ∧ ¬T ∧ ¬E. Da gir også raden 000 normal flow, og resten av tabellen er lik. Si hvilken tolkning du bruker.

*Merknad: «8-byte packet» er en skrivefeil i originalen. Pakken har 3 + 5 = 8 biter.*

*Kilde: egen løsning, ingen offisiell fasit for A4. Kontroll: tabellen og forenklingen er regnet ut med eget skript.*

tasks.d:
**2 Resolution in propositional logic**

Convert each of the following sentences to their Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF).

a) A ∨ (B ∧ C ∧ ¬D)

b) ¬(A ⇒ ¬B) ∧ ¬(C ⇒ ¬D)

c) ¬((A ⇒ B) ∧ (C ⇒ D))

d) (A ∧ B) ∨ (C ⇒ D)

e) A ⇔ (B ⇒ ¬C)
tasks.fasit:
**a) (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C) ∧ (A ∨ ¬D)**

**b) A ∧ B ∧ C ∧ D**

**c) (A ∨ C) ∧ (A ∨ ¬D) ∧ (¬B ∨ C) ∧ (¬B ∨ ¬D)**

**d) (A ∨ ¬C ∨ D) ∧ (B ∨ ¬C ∨ D)**

**e) (¬A ∨ ¬B ∨ ¬C) ∧ (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C)**

Rekkefølgen er alltid: fjern ⇔, fjern ⇒, flytt ¬ innover (De Morgan, double negation), distribuer ∨ over ∧.

- **a)** Distribusjon: A ∨ (B ∧ C ∧ ¬D) ≡ (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C) ∧ (A ∨ ¬D).
- **b)** ¬(A ⇒ ¬B) ≡ ¬(¬A ∨ ¬B) ≡ A ∧ B (implication elimination, De Morgan, double negation). Det samme gir C ∧ D.
- **c)** De Morgan: ¬(A ⇒ B) ∨ ¬(C ⇒ D) ≡ (A ∧ ¬B) ∨ (C ∧ ¬D). Distribusjon gir de fire klausulene.
- **d)** C ⇒ D ≡ ¬C ∨ D, så (A ∧ B) ∨ ¬C ∨ D. Distribusjon gir to klausuler.
- **e)** A ⇔ (¬B ∨ ¬C) ≡ (¬A ∨ ¬B ∨ ¬C) ∧ (¬(¬B ∨ ¬C) ∨ A) ≡ (¬A ∨ ¬B ∨ ¬C) ∧ ((B ∧ C) ∨ A). Distribusjon gir (A ∨ B) ∧ (A ∨ C).

Vanlig feil: å distribuere før negasjonen er flyttet inn, eller å glemme å bytte ∧ og ∨ i De Morgan.

*Kilde: notatet til E12, Fasit Øv selv 1 (egen løsning, ingen offisiell fasit for A4). Kontroll: hver CNF har samme sannhetstabell som originalen (alle 16 rader, eget skript).*

tasks.d:
Consider the following knowledge:

If the weather is both Sunny and Warm, then I Enjoy. If the weather is both Warm and Nice (not Raining), then I pick up Berries. If it is Raining, then I won’t pick up Berries. If it is Raining, then I will get wet. It is Warm. It is Raining. It is Sunny.

**Build a knowledge base** and **prove or disprove** the following statements using **resolution**:

(*Q*<sub>1</sub>) I won’t pick up Berries

(*Q*<sub>2</sub>) I will Enjoy

(*Q*<sub>3</sub>) I will get wet

*Hint: we suggest you use either complete words or the initial letter of each condition as your symbols.*
f: Q1: bevis eller motbevis med resolution
Q2: bevis eller motbevis med resolution
Q3: bevis eller motbevis med resolution
tasks.fasit:
**KB:** Sunny ∧ Warm ⇒ Enjoy, Warm ∧ ¬Raining ⇒ Berries, Raining ⇒ ¬Berries, Raining ⇒ Wet, Warm, Raining, Sunny. «Nice» er ¬Raining.

**Q1, Q2 og Q3 kan alle bevises.** KB ⊨ ¬Berries, KB ⊨ Enjoy og KB ⊨ Wet.

KB i CNF:

1. ¬Sunny ∨ ¬Warm ∨ Enjoy
2. ¬Warm ∨ Raining ∨ Berries
3. ¬Raining ∨ ¬Berries
4. ¬Raining ∨ Wet
5. Warm
6. Raining
7. Sunny

Resolution refutation: legg til negasjonen av målet og utled den tomme klausulen □.

**Q1: I won't pick up Berries** (mål ¬Berries)
- 8. Berries (negert mål)
- 9. ¬Raining (3 og 8)
- 10. □ (6 og 9)

**Q2: I will Enjoy**
- 8. ¬Enjoy (negert mål)
- 9. ¬Sunny ∨ ¬Warm (1 og 8)
- 10. ¬Warm (7 og 9)
- 11. □ (5 og 10)

**Q3: I will get wet**
- 8. ¬Wet (negert mål)
- 9. ¬Raining (4 og 8)
- 10. □ (6 og 9)

Klausul 2 trengs ikke, fordi det regner. KB har nøyaktig én modell: Sunny, Warm, Raining, Enjoy, Wet og ¬Berries.

Vanlig feil: å legge til målet selv i stedet for negasjonen.

*Kilde: notatet til E12, Fasit Øv selv 2 (egen løsning, ingen offisiell fasit for A4). Kontroll: model checking med eget skript gir det samme.*

tasks.d:
**3 Representation in First-Order Logic (FOL)**

Question taken from AIMA 3rd edition.

Consider the following vocabulary:

1. *Occupation*(*p*, *o*) is a predicate where person *p* has occupation *o*
2. *Customer*(*p*<sub>1</sub>, *p*<sub>2</sub>) is a predicate where person *p*<sub>1</sub> is a customer of person *p*<sub>2</sub>
3. *Boss*(*p*<sub>1</sub>, *p*<sub>2</sub>) is a predicate where person *p*<sub>1</sub> is a boss of person *p*<sub>2</sub>
4. *Doctor*, *Surgeon*, *Lawyer*, *Actor* are constants denoting an occupation
5. *Emily*, *Joe* are constants denoting people

Use the symbols above to **write the following statements in FOL**:

a) Emily is either a surgeon or a lawyer

b) Joe is an actor, but he also holds another job

c) All surgeons are doctos

d) Joe does not have a lawyer (i.e. he’s not a customer of any lawyer)

e) Emily has a boss who is a lawyer

f) There exists a lawyer all of whose customers are doctors

g) Every surgeon has a lawyer
tasks.fasit:
- **a) Occupation(Emily, Surgeon) ∨ Occupation(Emily, Lawyer)**
- **b) Occupation(Joe, Actor) ∧ ∃o [Occupation(Joe, o) ∧ ¬(o = Actor)]**
- **c) ∀p [Occupation(p, Surgeon) ⇒ Occupation(p, Doctor)]**
- **d) ¬∃p [Customer(Joe, p) ∧ Occupation(p, Lawyer)]**
- **e) ∃p [Boss(p, Emily) ∧ Occupation(p, Lawyer)]**
- **f) ∃p [Occupation(p, Lawyer) ∧ ∀q (Customer(q, p) ⇒ Occupation(q, Doctor))]**
- **g) ∀p [Occupation(p, Surgeon) ⇒ ∃q (Occupation(q, Lawyer) ∧ Customer(p, q))]**

Kommentarer:
- a) «either … or» leses vanligvis inkluderende. Vil du ha eksklusiv eller, legg til ∧ ¬(Occupation(Emily, Surgeon) ∧ Occupation(Emily, Lawyer)).
- b) ¬(o = Actor) er det som gjør jobben til en *annen* jobb.
- d) kan like gjerne skrives ∀p [Customer(Joe, p) ⇒ ¬Occupation(p, Lawyer)] (De Morgan for kvantorer).
- f) og g) har to kvantorer. Rekkefølgen og parentesene bestemmer hvem som er advokat og hvem som er kunde.

Vanlig feil: ∧ under ∀ (c blir da «alle er kirurger og leger») og ⇒ under ∃ (e blir sann bare fordi noen ikke er sjefen til Emily).

*Kilde: notatet til E14 (A4 oppgave 3.1, eget forslag; ingen offisiell fasit).*

tasks.d:
Arithmetic assertions can be written using First Order Logic. For example, the statement for Succesor(*x*, *y*) can be defined as Succesor(*x*, *y*) ⇔ *x* = *y* + 1. You can make it even more complicated by using function notation:

Succesor(x, y) ⇔ = (x, +(y, 1)).

And you can go all the way to define it as an S-expression using Polish notation for it to be understood by a LISP compiler if you want:

(iff (succesor x y) (= x (+ y 1))),

although you probably do not want to do that. Instead, use the predicates provided below, plus the usual arithmetic operators (<, >, ≤, ≠, =, +, −, ×, /, …), biconditionals, and integer constants to **express the following statements in FOL**. a) *Divisible*(*x*, *y*): an integer number *x* is *divisible* by *y* if there is some integer *z* less than *x* such that *x* = *z* × *y*. b) *Even*(*x*): a number is *even* if and only if it is divisible by 2. c) *Odd*(*x*): a number is *odd* if it is not divisible by 2. d) *Odd*(*x*): a number is *odd* if it is the result of summing 1 to an *even* number. e) *Prime*(*x*): a number is *prime* if is divisible only by itself. f) There is only one even prime number. g) Every integer number is equal to a product of prime numbers (*Hint: you can use* ∏i=1k pk *to express a product of numbers, or use* … *to express a repeating pattern like* p1, …, pn *meaning* p1, p2, p3 *and on until* pn). *Merknad:* Originalen er unøyaktig i a) (med z < x er ingen tall delelig med 1), e) (alle tall er delelige med 1, og 1 er ikke et primtall) og hintet i g) (pk i produktet skal være pi). Fasiten bruker de vanlige definisjonene.
f: f) Bare ett partall er primtall
tasks.fasit:
- **a) ∀x, y [Divisible(x, y) ⇔ ∃z (x = z × y)]**
- **b) ∀x [Even(x) ⇔ Divisible(x, 2)]**
- **c) ∀x [Odd(x) ⇔ ¬Divisible(x, 2)]**
- **d) ∀x [Odd(x) ⇔ ∃y (Even(y) ∧ x = y + 1)]**
- **e) ∀x [Prime(x) ⇔ x > 1 ∧ ∀y ((y > 0 ∧ Divisible(x, y)) ⇒ (y = 1 ∨ y = x))]**
- **f) ∃x [Even(x) ∧ Prime(x) ∧ ∀y ((Even(y) ∧ Prime(y)) ⇒ y = x)]**
- **g) ∀x [x > 1 ⇒ ∃k ∃p₁ … ∃p<sub>k</sub> (Prime(p₁) ∧ … ∧ Prime(p<sub>k</sub>) ∧ x = ∏<sub>i=1</sub><sup>k</sup> p<sub>i</sub>)]**

Alle variablene står for heltall.

**Originalen har feil i definisjonene, og fasiten bruker de vanlige:**
- a) «some integer z less than x» er ikke med. Med z < x er ingen tall delelig med 1 (z = x er ikke mindre enn x), og 0 og negative tall gir rare svar. Den vanlige definisjonen er bare ∃z (x = z × y).
- e) «divisible only by itself» glemmer at alle tall er delelige med 1, og utelukker ikke 1. Et primtall er et tall x > 1 der de eneste positive divisorene er 1 og x.
- g) Hintet skriver ∏<sub>i=1</sub><sup>k</sup> p<sub>k</sub>. Det skal være p<sub>i</sub>, ellers ganges samme tall med seg selv k ganger. «Every integer» må også begrenses til x > 1: 0, 1 og negative tall er ikke produkter av primtall. ∃k ∃p₁ … ∃p<sub>k</sub> er et formelskjema (én formel for hver k) og ikke én FOL-setning, men hintet tillater «…». Én setning får du ved å kvantifisere over en kodet endelig sekvens s: ∀x [x > 1 ⇒ ∃s (∀i ((1 ≤ i ∧ i ≤ Len(s)) ⇒ Prime(s<sub>i</sub>)) ∧ x = Prod(s))]. I aritmetikk kan Len, s<sub>i</sub> og Prod defineres med Gödels β-funksjon.

f) sier at det finnes nøyaktig ett tall som er både partall og primtall (det er 2). Uten ∀y-delen sier setningen bare at det finnes minst ett.

c) og d) er to definisjoner av samme predikat. For heltall er de ekvivalente.

*Kilde: egen løsning, ingen offisiell fasit for A4.*

tasks.d:
A new niche market has been discovered and some of your friends had the idea of developing a girl group K-Pop recommender system. Instead of using machine learning (as they think doing so may include bias in the data), they decided that going for a rule-based system was a better approach. This is what they said about it:

- All users who like *GG* are known as *Sone*, and therefore all *Sone* like *GG*
- All users who like *RV* are known as *Reveluvs*, and therefore all *Reveluvs* like *RV*
- All users who like *BP* are known as *Blinks*, and therefore all *Blinks* like *BP*
- All users who identify as *Reveluvs* will always like *Ballads*
- All users who identify as *Blinks* will always like *Dance*
- All users who like both *Dance* and *Ballads* will always like *CH*
- All users who like both *Drama* and *Ballads* will always like *HE*
- For all users who identify as *Sone*, the following holds:
  - If they like *Electro*, they will always like *DJH*
  - If they like *Drama*, they will always like *SEO*
  - If they like *Ballads*, they will always like *TAE*

You start to think if going with Machine Learning could result in less bias than using such rules, but you love your friends and carry on with their business idea. Your task is then to:

a) **Generate the knowledge base** by converting each rule to symbolic form.

b) Using **resolution**, **prove or disprove** (by showing the complete process) that if a new user *u*<sub>1</sub> is a fan of *GG* and identifies as *Reveluv*, then *TAE* will be a good recommendation.

c) Considering the same user *u*<sub>1</sub>, **prove or disprove** that *HE* will be a good recommendation.

d) Given what you know, if another user *u*<sub>2</sub> claims to be a *Sone*, a *Reveluv*, a *Blink*, and likes *Drama*; what are the possible artists and genre recommendations the system will provide?

*Hint: Consider using predicates to indicate that a user likes something (e.g. Electro(x)) instead of using likes(x, y) as a function.*
